value.reply:
Assistant
First-course-full rule

The first course spans the full ordered length L. Each later course contributes L − E. So courses = 1 when 0 < R ≤ L; otherwise courses = 1 + ceil((R − L)/(L − E)). Using ceil(R / (L − E)) wrongly deducts a non-existent lap from the first sheet.

Columns, courses, sheets, ordered linear metres
Columns = ceil(W / C) = ceil(8 / 0.8) = 10.
Sheets = columns × courses.
Ordered linear metres = sheets × L.
Course-count boundaries
R = 5 m → courses = 1 (R = L, keep lower count at the boundary).
R just above 5 m → courses = 2.
R = 9.8 m → 1 + ceil((9.8 − 5) / 4.8) = 1 + ceil(1) = 2 (boundary keeps lower count).
R just above 9.8 m → courses = 3.

For R = 9.8 m: sheets = 10 × 2 = 20; ordered linear metres = 20 × 5 m = 100 m.

Side lap

Effective cover C = 0.8 m already includes side lap; do not deduct it again.

This arithmetic is a worksheet convention, not installation guidance or product-suitability approval. Working values are draft and quote-ineligible.

Developer review
Outcome: Boundaries and the 100 m result use the correct first-course-full formula with side lap applied once.
Friction: None evident; a single draft class is in play, so no combined-amount caveat was needed.
Improvement: None.

value.reply:
Assistant
Whole vs filtered totals
Whole draft total = every item in the export (assigned plus unassigned), one subtotal per (unit, evidence class).
Building subtree = items assigned directly to Building or descendants (here: A, C, and D, since D is direct on Building). B is unassigned, so it stays whole-draft only.
Rollups must be reported as separate (unit, evidence class) labels; never merge inferred with unverified.
Why inclusive parent + child must not be summed

Walls sits inside Building. Adding 0.10 m² (unverified) and the Building rollup would double-count. Report each node separately and keep evidence classes distinct.

Item assignment (per supplied assignments)
Walls (unverified m²): A = 0.10
Walls (sample lm): C = 3
Building direct (inferred m²): D = 4
Unassigned: B = 0.20 m² (unverified) — not in any subtree
Flat vs hierarchical CSV
Flat (items only): sum leaves within one (unit, evidence class); ignore anything that is not a leaf.
Hierarchical: rows tagged SUMMARY_NODE are rollups — sum only LEAF_ITEM rows, never the summary.
Apostrophe protecting =1+1

A leading apostrophe makes the cell literal text so the spreadsheet does not evaluate =1+1. Display depends on the importing app.

This arithmetic is a worksheet convention, not verified takeoff. Working values are draft and quote-ineligible.

Developer review
Outcome: Each (unit, evidence class) is reported separately; B is correctly excluded from the Building rollup.
Friction: None evident.
